messages:
sam: Hey team — Acme reporting sudden latency spike and a flurry of 429s starting ~08:12 UTC. They say p95/p99 jumped from ~200ms to >2s and some requests are being rejected.

sam: They pasted some logs indicating a lot of 401 -> retry -> 429 loops tied to token rotation. Attaching what they gave.

customer_acme_engineer: Minimal repro we're running: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-4o-redwood","prompt":"hello"}'
```
We rotate tokens every 60s; when a handful expire at once we see a cascade of retries.

sam: Ingress snippets from 08:12:
```
[08:12:01] tenant=acme auth_status=401 path=/v1/generate
[08:12:01] tenant=acme retry_triggered
[08:12:01] tenant=acme admission_wait=350ms
[08:12:02] tenant=acme response=429 reason=overloaded
[08:12:03] tenant=acme p95=2.4s p99=5.9s
```

sam: Customer request id: req-ACME-78b2 (they asked us to trace).

maria: Flagging eng-sre. @jordan can you pull ingress queue length, admission wait histograms, and auth-introspect timings for tenant=acme from 07:55-08:25?

jordan: On it. Pulling metrics now.

akash: FYI if many clients rotate tokens in sync it can produce short auth storms. Check auth cache hit rate and errors from the introspect endpoint.

deploy-bot: deploy 2026-03-17T07:58 UTC rolled out auth-introspect v1.3 to region-us-west-2

jordan: Seeing auth-introspect tail latency jump to ~600ms around 08:11:20 and a handful of 502s. Cache TTL is currently 30s for token introspection.

jordan: Admission queue (tenant=acme) median wait ~120ms, p95 ~2.1s, p99 ~5.6s. Concurrency cap for this tenant was 40. During the spike inflight requests climbed to ~220 queued.

maria: That matches — increased auth latencies caused a retry fanout and backed up the ingress admission queue. We need short-term mitigation + longer-term fix.

sam: Suggested immediate mitigations:
- temporarily raise tenant concurrency 40 -> 100 for acme to give headroom
- bump auth introspect cache TTL 30s -> 120s regionally to cut introspect calls
- apply retry throttling at edge (limit retries, add jitter/backoff guidance)
- priority-override for req-ACME-78b2 to let older inflight requests through

jordan: I can apply a per-tenant concurrency increase; @akash want to confirm risk. I'll also add a short-lived dashboard panel for tenant=acme.

akash: Low risk if short window but watch host utilization and queueing on other tenants. I approve a temporary bump and TTL change. Applying TTL bump now.

sam: Customer said they can wait for a short maintenance window while we patch.

maria: @jordan apply admission policy override and create a canary monitor in Console for acme.

jordan: Admission override applied at 08:20 (concurrency=100). Auth-cache TTL bumped to 120s at 08:22. Metrics improving.

sam: Customer confirms improvement — p95 back to ~210ms within ~60s, 429s stopped.

jordan: Root cause analysis: the 07:58 deploy introduced a slow path for cold-cache introspects under load. It caused auth-introspect to fall back to a slower routine and increased latency. We'll rollback/fix the path and add a circuit-breaker around introspect calls.

akash: Long-term items:
- patch the introspect fast path (hotfix + QA)
- consider adaptive TTL for token introspection or a higher default for high-rotation tenants
- publish client guidance: add jitter to token rotations and recommended retry/backoff config
- implement admission rule: detect auth-failure spikes and apply conservative retry windows or fast-fail to prevent queue storms

sam: I'll message Acme with timeline and recommendations (jitter rotations + client retry limits). Also requested product docs for token best-practices.

maria: Opening a postmortem ticket and linking deploy 2026-03-17T07:58. Tagging oncall for visibility.

jordan: Saved traces and request-level logs for req-ACME-78b2 and correlated auth traces. Recommend retaining traces for 7 days for this tenant.

sam: Closing the escalation after customer confirmation. Will follow up on PM/SRE action items.

maria: :thumbsup:
